title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
blurb: A shepherd boy plays a trick twice. The third time is real.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… on a green hillside above a little village, there lived a boy whose job was to watch the sheep.

[gently] Every morning he walked them up the hill. Every evening he walked them down again. [short pause] And in between… there was nothing to do at all.

[thoughtful] The sheep ate grass. The clouds went by. The boy was very, very bored.

[mischievously] Then one afternoon, an idea came to him. A funny one. A naughty one.

[excited] He stood up on the highest rock, filled his chest with air, and shouted down at the village — [loudly] “WOLF! A wolf! A wolf is among the sheep!”

[excited] And oh, the village came RUNNING. The baker came with his rolling pin. The farmer came with his stick. Mothers came, and grandfathers came, all puffing up the steep hill.

[laughs] And when they reached the top… the boy was rolling in the grass, laughing at them.

[annoyed] “There is no wolf,” he giggled. “I made it up.”

[firmly] The villagers went back down the hill. They did not think it was funny.

[amused] A few days later, the boy was bored again. [short pause] And he did it again.

[loudly] “WOLF! WOLF! It is taking a lamb!”

[annoyed] Up came the village a second time, slower now, out of breath. And again they found nothing but sheep, and grass, and a laughing boy.

[firmly] “Do not call us again,” said the farmer quietly, “unless it is true.”

[softly] The sun went down. The sky turned deep and blue, and the hillside grew cold.

[whispers] And then… the sheep stopped eating. [short pause] All of them. All at once. Their heads came up together, and they stared at the dark line of the trees.

[worried] Something was moving there. Something grey. Something low.

The boy saw the eyes first. Then the shape. [surprised] A wolf — a real one — slipping out of the wood towards his flock.

[loudly] He ran to his rock and he shouted with all his heart. “WOLF! Please! There is a WOLF!”

[sad] And down in the village… they heard him. [short pause] And nobody came.

[gently] The boy shouted until his voice went thin. He shouted until the stars came out. And the wolf took what it wanted, and went back into the trees.

[softly] In the morning the old farmer climbed the hill and found the boy sitting quietly among the sheep that were left.

[gently] “We did hear you,” the farmer said. [short pause] “But when someone has told you a lie twice… the truth sounds just the same.”
